slides.title: AI Updates DataBricks KARL KARL - Knowledge Agents
slides.text: AI Updates DataBricks KARL KARL - Knowledge Agents via Reinforcement Learning From Static Skill.md to Reinforcement Learning System generates its own synthetic training problems based on a set of documents An agent attempts to solve these problems by searching documents. It records its "trajectory" Only the most successful trajectories are used to update the model's weights. This "bakes" the search intelligence directly into the AI's neural network rather than relying on a prompt KARL uses parallel reasoning attempts (multiple "rollouts") to verify and aggregate the best possible answer KARL reportedly outperforms larger models like Claude 4.6 and GPT-5.2 in specific knowledge-retrieval tasks while remaining cheaper and faster Intelligence gained through KARL can be distilled into smaller, "student" models, significantly boosting their performance https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OGT3NoFo-qg https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.05218 https://www.databricks.com/blog/meet-karl-faster-agent-enterprise-knowledge-powered-custom-rl

slides.title: Claude Code Scheduling Claude scheduled tasks The first
slides.text: Claude Code Scheduling Claude scheduled tasks The first method works within Claude Desktop's co-work tab, running in a VM sandbox with access to external connectors but limited local file access. The second runs in Claude Desktop's code tab with full local system access including files, terminal, and git. The third uses the /loop slash command in Claude Code CLI for short-term tasks up to 3 days, tied to specific sessions. The fourth method leverages GitHub Actions for repository-focused automation that doesn't require keeping your computer on. Key limitations include most methods requiring the desktop app to remain open, potential permission prompts, and stateless execution unless you implement memory through JSON files. The choice depends on your time horizon and task type: .. use /loop for short development tasks, .. desktop scheduling for long-running persistent automation, .. and consider access requirements when choosing between co-work and code tabs Agent /loop command to schedule tasks within session Running every 10 minutes by default for up to 3 days Users can set reminders and recurring tasks using natural language, such as "remind me at 10:23 AM" or "check my ClickUp every 10 minutes." Limitation - the features works only within the same session. It requires the terminal window and computer to stay open, doesn't survive restarts, and expires after 3 days. The feature works across VS Code, terminal, and desktop app Claude Code Desktop actually offers more powerful scheduling that survives restarts and runs indefinitely, though it still requires the desktop app open. Super Nested Claude Code A nested Claude Code workflow in tmux on macOS Coordinates multiple terminals for parallel AI-assisted development A central controller assigns subtasks across terminals, letting developers state high-level goals while Claude manages planning and execution steps Examples include a multi-terminal 3D galaxy project in 3JS and visualizing micro GPT training with dedicated panes for backend, charts, and dashboards. The system boosts productivity but currently depends on macOS, tmux, and a non-trivial setup. https://www.geeky-gadgets.com/nested-claude-code-tmux/

slides.title: Claude Code - Tool Search & Calling Use
slides.text: Claude Code - Tool Search & Calling Use Claude Code to automate model training https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jP6tN9JTtxE Automate machine learning model training using three tools working together: Claude Code as an AI agent, HuggingFace Jobs for cloud GPU compute, and Tracko for experiment tracking. The presenter modifies Andre Karpathy's nano GPT repository to train a GPT2-level model, integrating Tracko to log metrics and generate alerts when validation loss increases. Claude Code acts as an autonomous ML researcher, systematically testing different learning rates starting from 1.0 and automatically terminating unstable training runs based on Tracko alerts. The system successfully found an optimal learning rate of 0.1 after canceling higher learning rate experiments that showed instability. This approach enables efficient autonomous hyperparameter optimization while minimizing cloud compute costs by quickly terminating unsuccessful experiments. Anthropic tool search and calling Reduce token usage by up to 85% https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7OCrqyGMeY Tool search allows agents to discover and load tools on-demand rather than loading everything upfront, significantly reducing context usage. Programmatic tool calling enables agents to write and execute Python scripts in sandboxes to handle complex multi-step tasks more efficiently than traditional sequential tool calls. The video demonstrates these patterns in a custom system using Qwen 3.5 model, showing how these aren't exclusive to Claude The system uses Docker containers for secure code execution with a tool bridge architecture that prevents direct internet access while enabling communication with external services through authenticated calls. Concentrate on Building Skills https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wqH1hTkA6qg Skills are markdown instruction files to provide expertise on-demand, functioning like employee playbooks Skills are modular and "progressively disclosed" - Claude only loads relevant skills when needed. Common Mistakes when Using Skills First Mistake - installing too many skills (50-200) which creates noise in Claude's 15,000 chars system prompt budget and leads to ambiguous skill selection. Solution - use only 20-30 specific, well-built skills Second Mistake - installing generic marketplace skills without customization, resulting in generic output. Solution - add reference files with brand guidelines and examples Third Mistake - cram everything into a single skill.md file instead of using proper folder structure with separate reference files, making debugging difficult and wasting context tokens https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CXeCIgc982I Prompt Engineering => Context Engineering => Workflows (Skill Creator)

slides.title: Claude Code is NOT Open Source Claude Code
slides.text: Claude Code is NOT Open Source Claude Code and Claude models are NOT open source Under the hood, Claude Code is just a Claude model (e.g., a Sonnet or Opus “thinking” variant) prompted and tooled for software tasks: reading/editing code, explaining errors, designing APIs, etc. The model performs step-by-step reasoning internally (especially in “thinking”/reasoning modes), which improves multi-step tasks like debugging or refactoring, but those thoughts are not a symbolic program or fixed algorithm—just very large pattern-based inference over its training data plus your prompt The Claude base model has broad capabilities (coding, natural language, reasoning) baked into its weights; those aren’t modular plug‑ins you can see or toggle Platforms (like Claude Code) then layer “skills” on top by using specialized system prompts (e.g., “act as a software engineer”), and enabling tools such as code execution, browsing, file and repo access, or chart/image creation By default, Claude Code runs in the cloud on Anthropic or partner infrastructure; your prompts and code are sent to remote servers for inference Additional “skills” like web browsing, Deep Research, and code sandboxes are also cloud services, not something the model does purely on your local machine You can integrate Claude via API into your own stack, but the core model execution still happens on remote cloud Claude Code is better than Cline Cline, by design, is more model‑agnostic and prompt‑driven Claude Code (CC) is Anthropic specific. It was released in Feb 2025. Over the whole year it was tuned to work with Claude models and tools, and models were tuned to work with CC So even if you try to use the same Opus model with both Cline and CC, the CC experience will be “smoother” because of better orchestration, tighter tool contracts, better defaults, better chunking and truncation. And the Claude models are trained to use  the Claude tools effectively https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code https://www.anthropic.com/news/enabling-claude-code-to-work-more-autonomously Anthropic uses large, sophisticated system prompts plus tool definitions to define how Claude behaves in each product, and CC has its own agent spec layered on top of the base model So CC is basically talking to the specialized agent in the cloud. A public analysis of Claude’s system prompts shows Anthropic routinely bakes workflows, safety rules, and UX behaviors directly into long system messages (tens of thousands of tokens), rather than leaving everything to the user; The tool definitions alone are ~11k tokens, and Anthropic exposes multiple “system prompt methods” (base agent prompt, user‑customizable extra prompt, etc.), which strongly suggests a nontrivial internal prompt stack optimized for dev workflows Claude Code is better than Cline

slides.title: Superpowers Superpowers GitHub repo for AI Coding Agents
slides.text: Superpowers Superpowers GitHub repo for AI Coding Agents https://github.com/obra/superpowers http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7cOAayWzYDY /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace A fully autonomous software development workflow for AI coding agents Unlike traditional "spec-driven" tools like OpenSpec or SpecKit, which primarily focus on turning conversations into task lists, Superpowers manages the entire engineering lifecycle. It guides agents through brainstorming, design generation, technical specification, and detailed implementation planning Key features include the ability to handle non-linear tasks, reduce hallucinations by keeping models focused on specific steps, and the integration of "sub-agents" to execute parallel implementation plans Users can easily install Superpowers as a plugin within coding environments like Cursor or Claude Code Ultimately, the toolkit aims to replace "vibe coding" with a structured, reliable workflow that produces professional-grade, bug-free results

slides.title: OpenClaw Memory OpenClaw 3-Layer Memory Architecture Layer 1
slides.text: OpenClaw Memory OpenClaw 3-Layer Memory Architecture Layer 1 - core identity (the "Soul") - in he root of workspace: files: soul.md, agents.md, memory.md, and user.md only the owner can edit the identiy files Layer 2 - long-term recall - in "Memory" folder files - Daily logs (dated `YYYY-MM-DD.md`) and specific topic files (e.g., ` onboarding.md `) short (under 4KB) summaries and "breadcrumbs" Layer 3 - Deep References (The Library) in "Reference" folder files - full documents and long-form histories Enable `memory_flush` in the config file to stop immediate context loss on resets. Write memory files in plain, natural language https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f8LJBh1AtKg

slides.title: Moonshots - about OpenClaw OpenClaw is an open-source,
slides.text: Moonshots - about OpenClaw OpenClaw is an open-source, self-improving AI agent that runs locally on your computer 24/7, with no token limits or cloud costs Alex Finn runs four agents (Henry, Ralph, Charlie, Scout) organized like a business hierarchy, with Henry (Claude Opus) as chief of staff Local hardware, especially Apple devices with unified memory architecture, is strongly preferred over virtual private servers for speed, security, and cost OAuth lets you connect existing ChatGPT subscriptions to OpenClaw instead of paying per token Key use cases include autonomous software development, content pipelines, and research automation Memory is stored in plain markdown files; agents can design and fix their own memory systems A recent security vulnerability allowed websites to hijack agents via JavaScript; patched within 24 hours Best starting tip: use reverse prompting - tell your agent your goals and ask it what it should do next https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qP73cGLQmCU https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d__HRChE2ZE

slides.title: AI is transforming education AI is fundamentally transforming
slides.text: AI is transforming education AI is fundamentally transforming education and learning https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WzOXDIWxVeM Traditional courses are becoming obsolete as AI agents can now handle most learning tasks automatically Instead of consuming pre-made content, learners will receive personalized, on-demand lessons generated by AI. New learning model focuses on "loops" rather than linear curricula: goal-setting tiny actions feedback proof of completion next steps Shift from content delivery to live facilitation and community accountability Rather than learning how to do things, people now tell AI what they want accomplished The value lies in guided environments where people actually implement and change behavior , not just consume information. Communities become essential for accountability , requiring members to show what they've started, built, and shipped rather than just completing courses. The transformation moves educators from creators to conductors , focusing on practical implementation over knowledge transfer

slides.text: AI Updates Anthropic sues Pentagon Anthropic has filed a federal lawsuit against the U.S. Department of Defense after the Pentagon designated the AI company a “supply-chain risk” Anthropic has launched Claude Marketplace This new platform allows enterprise customers with existing Anthropic spending commitments to purchase third-party applications powered by Claude Such as tools from GitLab, Harvey, Replit, Snowflake, and others, with billing handled directly through Anthropic The goal is to simplify procurement and consolidate AI spending while making it easier for companies to access specialized Claude-powered tools built by partners for specific industries and workflows. The move signals that Anthropic sees continued value in SaaS applications enhanced with AI rather than fully replacing them with custom AI workflows Claude Marketplace could allow enterprises to use Claude as a central orchestrator that connects to approved tools and services, though its success will depend on whether businesses adopt the marketplace instead of continuing to build their own AI integrations or using existing partner APIs OpenAI revises military AI deal with US Government after criticism that the original deal was rushed and lacked clear safeguards The updated terms explicitly prohibit using OpenAI’s systems for domestic surveillance of U.S. citizens and require additional approval before intelligence agencies like the NSA can use the technology.

slides.title: Intel 18A Manufacturing Process 2021: Intel announces “5
slides.text: Intel 18A Manufacturing Process 2021: Intel announces “5 nodes in 4 years” (Intel 4, 3, 20A, 18A), with RibbonFET and PowerVia planned for 20A/18A 2022–2023: Intel 4 and then Intel 3 enter production for Meteor Lake client and Xeon data‑center chips March 2023: Intel finalizes process rules for Intel 20A and 18A Mid‑2023: PowerVia test chips demonstrate working backside power delivery 2024: Intel deprioritizes 20A for high‑volume client products (Arrow Lake leans heavily on TSMC), using 20A mainly as a learning node 2025: Intel 18A achieves production‑viable defect density and begins risk/early production January 2026: Intel 18A enters high‑volume production; first 18A‑based Core Ultra Series 3 mobile CPUs are announced, with systems shipping during 2026 Intel 18A process, RibbonFET, PowerVia The "18A" name refers to 1.8 nm RibbonFET - new type of transistor where the gate surrounds the channel on all sides. This replaces the older "FinFET" design to provide better control over electricity, reducing leaks and heat while allowing the chips to get even smaller PowerVia (moving power delivery to the back of the chip) - reduces power loss by 30% and allows for much higher transistor density While TSMC and Samsung are working on similar backside power technologies, they aren't expected to release them until late 2026 or 2027. Intel, however, is already launching products using 18A in 2026. Intel Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake architecture) Major manufacturers like Acer, Dell, and Samsung are already releasing laptops with these processors Intel is also targeting the handheld gaming market, claiming a 70% performance boost for portable devices Ultimately, the 18A process is Intel’s "all-in" bet to reclaim its crown as the world's leading chipmaker

slides.title: Leopold Aschenbrenner Investments $255 Mln into $5.5 Bln
slides.text: Leopold Aschenbrenner Investments $255 Mln into $5.5 Bln in ~1.5 years Leopold Aschenbrenner, - 24 y.old investor SITUATIONAL AWARENESS LP (SALP) - hedge fund with 2 clients https://situationalawarenesslp.com His investment strategy is laid out in his 165‑page essay “Situational Awareness,” where he predicts AGI by 2027 how the AI boom will unfold https://situational-awareness.ai/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/situationalawareness.pdf . He is a former OpenAI researcher, famously fired after ~ 1 year Leopold first rode the GPU/chip boom but is now pivoting from “chips to infrastructure.” He has exited major chip names like Nvidia, Broadcom, TSMC, and Micron, arguing that by 2025–2026 the market will have fully priced in GPUs He believes the new bottleneck is energy and infrastructure - so his largest new positions are highly concentrated bets on power and infrastructure The top holding is Bloom Energy, around 20% of the portfolio, which makes modular solid oxide fuel‑cell systems that can generate electricity from natural gas on‑site next to data centers, bypassing stressed local grids He also invests heavily in CoreWeave, a “neo‑cloud” provider that buys GPUs and handles all the painful physical work - racks, power, cooling, engineering - for AI labs He also invests in Core Scientific - a major supplier that helps set up energy grids for CoreWeave The hosts highlight that this lets him sidestep slow, painful permitting: instead of waiting years for grid access like big tech companies, he buys firms that already have it and repurposes them. They admire the simplicity of his logic—Bitcoin miners already have energy and space, AI desperately needs energy and space—and how consistently his earlier GPU thesis has played out. Leopold shorted Infosys, an Indian IT outsourcing company whose model relies on cheap human labor. He’s betting that modern AI coding and IT tools are now good enough to automate much of this work, making such labor‑arbitrage businesses structurally vulnerable. AGI‑by‑2027 prediction, noting a Polymarket contract that puts the probability of OpenAI declaring AGI before 2027 at around 13%. They suggest his investment thesis on infrastructure may still be right even if his timing on AGI is off, and emphasize that so far he has correctly anticipated both the GPU rush and, they think, the emerging energy‑infrastructure rush. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=04Kutj1vAiw He has bought sizable stakes in Bitcoin mining companies, not for crypto, but for their two scarce assets: power hookups and permitted industrial real estate. The thesis is that these miners can pivot their sites from mining to AI data centers (or sell rights/permits), giving Leopold indirect exposure to critical energy and land

slides.title: Autoresearch from Andrej Karpathy Autoresearch from Andrej Karpathy
slides.text: Autoresearch from Andrej Karpathy Autoresearch from Andrej Karpathy Andrej Karpathy recently introduced autoresearch, an open-source project that transforms a single GPU into an autonomous AI research lab The system uses an AI agent to conduct overnight LLM training experiments without human intervention The agent iteratively modifies a single training file, runs five-minute experiments on a nanochat model, and evaluates performance using validation bits per byte By fixing the time budget, the agent can complete approximately twelve experiments per hour, searching for the most efficient model architecture and hyperparameters for the specific hardware This project demonstrates a shift toward agentic engineering, where AI researchers move from manual coding to overseeing autonomous agents that handle the low-level iteration and optimization of neural networks https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch https://x.com/karpathy https://www.youtube.com/shorts/g7V0UJv9gT4 https://garryslist.org/posts/karpathy-just-turned-one-gpu-into-a-research-lab-f55754a6 Modeling a fruit fly brain wired as in nature, inside a 3D simulated fly body so behaviors emerge from biology, not trained AI This “uploaded” animal walks and reacts realistically In 1 year: from a 302‑neuron worm to a ~125k‑neuron fly Humans ~ 30...80 Bln (only !!) https://flywire.ai https://x.com/michaelandregg/status/2030764512488677736 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N2ccho6ug1w - video

slides.title: Alibaba’s Qwen Team Restructuring Massive leadership exodus from
slides.text: Alibaba’s Qwen Team Restructuring Massive leadership exodus from Alibaba’s Qwen team Tech lead Junyang Lynn and several core contributors resigned after a corporate restructuring that shifted the team from a fast-moving, vertically integrated unit to a fragmented, "horizontal" module system managed by Alibaba Cloud This "geminification" prioritizes commercial applications over the development of underlying open-source model capabilities. Qwen is currently the world’s most downloaded open-source model family, uniquely specializing in small, efficient language models that run on consumer hardware However, the intense "consumer AI war" in China against ByteDance has weakened Alibaba's incentive to give away high-performance models for free If Qwen stops its open-source output, it will leave a massive gap in the practical AI ecosystem that no other company is currently positioned to fill https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TJ5okrPNmWQ Alibaba Qwen 3.5 Medium This v.3.5 35-Bln outperforms v.3.0 235-Bln params Model efficiency is advancing faster than model scale.
